title: A generic constant sheaf on a normal Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $V$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], normal and integral [def-pc-integral-scheme] in the sense of [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois], with generic point $\eta$, function field $K=\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field], and generic inclusion $e:\operatorname{Spec}K\to V$. For a finite abelian group $M$, let $\underline M_V$ and $\underline M_K$ be the constant sheaves on the etale sites [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Then the natural map of etale sheaves $\underline M_V\to e_*\underline M_K$ is an isomorphism, where $e_*$ is the direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image].

proof.text:
Since a morphism of sheaves is an isomorphism once it is one on the objects of a basis of the site, it suffices to evaluate on an etale $W\to V$ with $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ affine and mapping into an affine open $V_0=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq V$; such $W$ cover every object of $V_{\Et}$. Then $A$ is a Noetherian domain with fraction field $K$, and $C$ is of finite type over $A$, hence Noetherian, so $W$ is Noetherian.
By [lem-fin-etale-normal-components], $W$ has finitely many
normal integral open-and-closed components $W_a=\operatorname{Spec}C_a$, each affine and etale over $V_0$.
Every nonempty $W_a$ dominates $V$, since its image is a nonempty
open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], and a nonempty open of the irreducible $V$ contains $\eta$. Moreover $A\to C_a$ is flat and $C_a$ is a domain, so every nonzero $a\in A$ (a nonzerodivisor) has nonzero image in $C_a$.
Its generic fibre $W_a\times_V\operatorname{Spec}K=\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_AC_a)$ is therefore nonempty and connected by [lem-weil-pbc-generic-fibre-localization-domain-irreducible]. Thus $W$ and $W_K=W\times_V\operatorname{Spec}K$ have the
same finite set of connected components, $W_a$ and $(W_a)_K$.
The sections of a constant sheaf $M$ on a connected scheme are
$M$, by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected].
Both groups of sections here are therefore $\prod_aM$, and
restriction along $W_K\to W$ sends constant sections to constant sections, so it is the identity on each factor.
By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $(e_*\underline M_K)(W)=\underline M_K(W_K)$, and these restriction maps are precisely the components of the natural map, which is therefore an isomorphism on this basis of the site.
